text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The government's 1997 budget proposals say companies that supply goods and services to the government are only obliged to pay VAT after the state pays its debts to the suppliers.
- Agriculture fund Fundo de Garantia Agricola will inject between seven and eight billion escudos into banking group Credito Agricola by the end of 1996, a source from the bank told the paper.
- Portuguese soldiers will leave for eastern Zaire on a humanitarian mission to help starving refugees.
- Official statistics indicate that the debt of the state health services rose by 62 billion escudos in 1996.
- The Bank of Portugal said the government must maintain tight control of 1997 salary rises in order to keep a lid on inflation.
- General-Inspectorate for Health is investigate the accounts and management of the Portugal League Against Cancer, a reliable source told the paper.
